predecessors.name: Kingdom of Lysimachus
predecessors.text: the Pergamon fortress and its district, part of Lysimachus's realm

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: most of the kingdom, the province of Asia, 129

successors.name: Kingdom of Pontus
successors.text: Phrygia, Pontus's share in Aquillius's division

successors.name: Kingdom of Cappadocia
successors.text: Cappadocia's share, not located on the page

ledger.x: 261: Eumenes I defeats Antiochus I near Sardis and makes Pergamon independent.

c. 230: Attalus I fights Antiochus Hierax. He 'fought Antiochus Hierax and his Gallic allies at Aphrodisium, in the east, near Sardis, and at the Harpasus in Caria'; the key battle is dated to spring 228 and the war to c. 230-227.
c. 227: the war ends. 'Attalus gained putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains' (tenuous).

c. 227: Attalus I's gains from Hierax. 'Attalus gained putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains'; the Pergamon page says the kingdom 'stretched over 143,000 square kilometres' after Hierax's death. Cliopatria shows only the 105-cell secure part from 225.

210: Aegina. Attalus I was elected a strategos for 210/209 in the Aetolian alliance; the island was 'acquired by Attalus as his base of operations in Greece' and kept after the Treaty of Phoenice (205). The page does not say from whom.
188: the Treaty of Apamea concludes the war.

133: Attalus III dies and bequeaths his kingdom to Rome ('exempted Pergamum and the Greek cities'); Aristonicus, 'claiming to be an illegitimate son of Eumenes II', takes the name Eumenes III and revolts, seizing Leucae, Samos, Myndus and Colophon in sea raids and Thyatira and Apollonis inland.
129: Rome makes the Pergamene kingdom the province of Asia.

wars.name: War of Attalus I against Antiochus Hierax
wars.outcome: Attalus won at Aphrodisium, near Sardis and the Harpasus and gained putative control of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus.

wars.name: War of Attalus I against Achaeus
wars.outcome: Achaeus shut Attalus up in Pergamon (223); Attalus retook the west in 218, Achaeus returned in 217; Antiochus III took Sardis in 214 and Attalus regained his lands after Achaeus' execution in 213.

wars.name: First Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Attalus fought on Rome's side with a minor part; Aegina was acquired as his base (210) and kept under the Treaty of Phoenice (205).

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War (Pergamene part)
wars.outcome: Magnesia (190) and the Treaty of Apamea (188): Antiochus III gave up Asia west of the Taurus; Eumenes II received a large part of Asia Minor and Rhodes the rest.

wars.name: Eumenes II against Prusias I of Bithynia
wars.outcome: 'He suffered an initial defeat, then won after Roman support allowed a counterattack' (183); no frontier changed.

wars.name: Eumenes II against Pharnaces I of Pontus
Revolt of Aristonicus
wars.outcome: A first Roman army was defeated in 131, a second force beat Aristonicus in 130 and Perperna starved him into submission; Aquillius divided the kingdom among Rome, Pontus and Cappadocia in 129.

certainty.note: No treaty line is described: the Treaty of Apamea gave regions, not a surveyed frontier, so every frontier is soft.
